rows.description: A child lines up which toy to tidy first or which drawing to finish before dinner, picking by what feels most urgent or fun. Ordering things is new, so the plan changes the moment something shinier appears.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Big task feels like a wall [Actor]
rows.description: A child looking at a full chapter or a project chart sees only its size and freezes or wanders off. Without a first small piece in view, the task feels impossible rather than merely long.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager writes study more as a plan and then sits with no idea where to begin. A goal without a first physical action such as solving five sums from chapter three leaves the mind with nothing to grip.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Splitting a project into checkable pieces [Response]
rows.description: A wise worker divides a large task into pieces that can each be finished in under an hour and ticks them off. Each completed piece gives real evidence of progress and lowers the dread of the whole.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Estimating time and the planning fallacy
rows.description: A team lead relies on a colleague's promised date and then has to reshuffle everything when it slips. Repeated optimism erodes trust more than an honest longer estimate would have.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child begins a craft kit or a diary with great excitement and drops it when the novelty fades. The joy is in beginning; the flat middle needs a tolerance for boredom that is still developing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, excitement, boredom

rows.description: A teenager has a guitar, a coding course and a fitness plan all begun and none completed. Each new idea feels more exciting than pushing an old one through its dull stretch, which quietly builds a self-image of a non-finisher.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Attention pulled by whatever is nearby [Actor]
rows.description: A young child starts putting on shoes, notices a toy and is soon playing on the floor with one shoe on. Attention follows the most interesting thing in view, and remembering the original goal is still fragile.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult waits for a clear desk, a full day and the right mood before starting a thesis chapter. Perfect conditions are a polite name for postponement, and they never quite arrive.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Warning early when a deadline will slip [Response]
rows.description: A responsible worker tells others as soon as a date looks unsafe, with a new realistic date and options. Early bad news can be planned around; late bad news is felt as a betrayal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
